fact: The National Information Technology Agency (NITA) put out its draft Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 and invited all stakeholders and the general public, including citizens, academia and the private sector, to make submissions in a public consultation announced on 2025-10-23 and set to run from 2025-11-19 to 2025-11-27 via the consultation document on its website.

Ghana's OGP Secretariat and Multi-Stakeholder Forum co-created the fifth Open Government Partnership National Action Plan (NAP 5) in 2023 with civil society organisations (including GACC, GII, CDD, IDEG and MFWA) and government agencies in consultative meetings and an October 2023 co-creation workshop, and the plan carries commitments on misinformation on digital platforms, on amending the Electronic Communications Act 2008, and on data sharing and open data (published 2023-12, event dated October 2023).
NITA invited ministries, assemblies, private sector, academia, civil society, development partners and the public to comment on the draft Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 from 19 to 27 November 2025.
The NCA held an inaugural stakeholder engagement with mobile terminal device manufacturers and dealers to design a new minimum specification for terminal devices.
The National Communications Authority had an ongoing public consultation on the Electronic Communications Bill, 2025, dated 16 October 2025 in the article's references.
Adomonline says the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations invited public comments on the draft MDHI Bill 2025, and GIMPA Law School filed a submission on 10 November 2025.

The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations says it began a two-day stakeholder meeting on 10 February 2026 in Accra to discuss, clause by clause, the inputs received in public consultations on the Draft Misinformation, Disinformation, Hate Speech and Publication of Other Information Bill.

fact: The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations received over 272 stakeholder memos on the draft amendment to the Cyber Security Act, 1038, in a public consultation from October to November 2025, and inaugurated a Cybersecurity Industry Forum on 11 December 2025.

The Media Foundation for West Africa says Ghana's communications ministry opened its 15 new digital governance bills, including the MDHI, Cybersecurity (Amendment) and Ghana Domain Name Registry bills of 2025, to public feedback, and submitted its comments while asking for a longer window.
The CSA invited cybersecurity professionals, service providers, civil society and the public to comment on the draft Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill, 2025, from 1 October to 14 November 2025.

The National Communications Authority held a two-day workshop on 9-10 May 2024 to review stakeholders' comments on its draft guidelines for publishing mobile tariffs and terms, with mobile network operators, consumer advocacy groups and the Ghana Chamber of Telecommunications taking part.
